accounts.intro: Import your bank's statement, match each line to what the books recorded, and see what is still to explain.
accounts.noBalance: No running balance on the statement
accounts.emptyBody: Add your bank account under Settings › Payment accounts, then import its statement here.

account.noStatement: No statement imported yet. Import one to start matching.

record.paymentHint: The payment takes this line's date, amount and reference, through this bank account, and is matched to it.
record.noCategories: Add an expense category under Settings first
record.voucherInTitle: Record money in to an account
record.voucherOutTitle: Record money out from an account
record.voucherInHint: For money in that isn't a customer's payment, such as interest, a loan or capital brought in. A receipt voucher is recorded on this line's date and matched to it.
record.voucherOutHint: For money out that isn't a supplier's payment or an expense, such as drawings, a loan repaid or tax paid. A journal is recorded on this line's date and matched to it.
record.advanceIn: {{amount}} left over is held as an advance from the customer
record.advanceOut: {{amount}} left over is held as an advance to the supplier
record.allAllocated: All of it settles what is due

lines.noSuggestion: Nothing in the books with this amount nearby
lines.unmatchedToast: Match undone; the line is back in To explain

emptyBody.unmatched: Every imported line is matched or excluded. Import the next statement when it comes.
emptyBody.matched: Lines matched to a payment, expense or voucher show here.
emptyBody.excluded: Lines you set aside as needing nothing in the books show here.

find.title: Find the record
find.subtitle: {{amount}} on {{date}}: payments and expenses on this account within a month
find.none: Nothing on this account near that date
find.amountDiffers: This is {{amount}}; the bank line is {{line}}. Only the same amount can be matched.

exclude.title: Exclude this line?
exclude.body: An excluded line needs nothing in the books, such as a transfer already recorded or a bank's own reversal. It stays out of the reconciliation until you include it again.

import.title: Import a statement into {{account}}
import.hint: Download the statement from your bank's net banking as Excel (.xlsx) or CSV. Lines already imported are skipped, and lines that clearly match a payment or expense are matched for you.
import.noAmount: Choose an amount column, or a debit or credit column.
import.noColumns: No date or amount column to read
import.dryRun: {{imported}} new, {{duplicates}} already imported, {{autoMatched}} will match on their own.
import.doneDetail: {{duplicates}} already there, {{autoMatched}} matched on their own

importFlow.wrongType: That kind of file can't be imported here. Use {{kinds}}.
importFlow.tooBig: The file is too large. It can be at most {{mb}} MB.
importFlow.empty: The file has nothing in it.
importFlow.webOnlyBody: Open Elixir Books on the web to import {{kinds}} files. What you import shows here too.
importFlow.headerAt_one: {{name}}: headings on row {{row}}, {{count}} row under them.
importFlow.headerAt_other: {{name}}: headings on row {{row}}, {{count}} rows under them.
importFlow.noHeader_one: {{name}}: no heading row found in {{count}} row. Choose each column.
importFlow.noHeader_other: {{name}}: no heading row found in {{count}} rows. Choose each column.
importFlow.checkFirst: Check the rows to see what the import will do.
importFlow.tooMany: More than {{max}} rows. Split the file and import it in parts.
importFlow.nothingBody: Check that the date and amount columns are the right ones.

brs.addCredits: Add: credited by the bank, not yet in the books
brs.lessDebits: Less: debited by the bank, not yet in the books
brs.statementBalanceOn: Balance as per bank statement on {{date}}
brs.addDeposits: Add: deposited, not yet credited by the bank
brs.lessPayments: Less: paid, not yet debited by the bank
brs.agreesHint: Every difference between the books and the bank is explained.
brs.differsHint: Something is still unexplained: a line matched to the wrong record, an amount typed differently, or an entry before the first imported statement.
brs.noBalance: The statement has no running balance, so the bank side can't be totalled. Import a statement with a balance column to compare.
brs.since: Records dated before {{date}}, the start of the first imported statement, are taken as cleared.

imports.emptyBody: Each statement you import shows here, and one imported by mistake can be undone.
imports.undoBody: Its {{count}} lines are taken away. Payments, expenses and vouchers they were matched to, or recorded from, stay in the books and can be matched again.
